deck.section.s2: Flagship offerings: agriculture, home equity, auto, and consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group)

abertura.alt01: Illustrative scene: female executive beside the catalisa logo carved in travertine
abertura.text03: Your customer understands the offer. Your team manages the transaction. Your brand builds the relationship.
abertura.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Sequences: 20 · executive · 22 slides; 40 · product · 67; 60 · technical · 89. Follow the tag in each note. Open with the relationship the institution builds with its customer. The offering combines clear terms, contracting channels, and operations that support the loan throughout its term. Catalisa delivers this under the buyer's brand, with Decision as the shared engine across credit products. To explain what the buyer is purchasing, describe a platform for configuring, distributing, and operating financial products, from customer engagement to portfolio management. Lead with the white-label proposition, available on-premises or as SaaS, with commercial responsibilities defined in the partnership.
contrato.text02: Every contract brings a transaction together.
contrato.text03: The customer reviews, accepts, and signs. The institution decides, authorizes, and services the loan, with documents, installments, and records supporting the relationship.
contrato.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Walk through both sides of the contract. The customer needs to understand the offer and each next step; the team needs to gather documents, apply policy, complete execution, and release funds. After disbursement, servicing continues through monitoring, installments, and collections. Explain that the platform also supports portfolio operations. Receivables financing makes that continuity tangible: a signed assignment, authorization of Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), monitoring, and incoming payments linked to the transaction.
portfolio.alt01: Illustrative scene: executive in an architectural setting with an orange bridge
portfolio.text02:
Your next offering
starts with your customer.
portfolio.text03: Banking and credit under your brand. Receivables, personal loans, and payroll-deductible loans expand your portfolio; agriculture, home equity, auto, and consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group) open four avenues for customer relationships.
portfolio.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Start with the needs served: liquidity, installment credit, asset-backed borrowing, and planned purchases. The Flagship Offerings chapter highlights agriculture, home equity, auto, and consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group). In Credit Products, each offering has its own data, calculations, instrument, and servicing. Consórcio sits alongside credit as a distinct form of planned purchasing. The shared foundation brings together Decision for credit, calculations, execution and documentation, the credit desk, and channels. Consórcio sales and support workflows serve both participants and representatives.
sua-marca.text05: Your brand and domain at every customer touchpoint.
sua-marca.text08: Products, policies, and workflows define each institution's operating environment.
sua-marca.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Present white-label as the core product proposition. Customers see the institution's brand and domain. Operators work with products, policies, and workflows organized in their own environment, with dedicated data, keys, and events. Establish ownership of the commercial relationship in the opening statement: the buyer brings its brand to the customer. Catalisa provides the platform that brings the offering together. Journeys, operational responsibilities, and the partnership structure are defined jointly for the selected offering.
banking.text02: Every relationship starts with an account.
banking.text03: Individuals and businesses open accounts under your brand. Balances, statements, and Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) keep the experience connected across mobile and desktop.
banking.alt01: White-label bank welcome screen for opening an individual or business account
banking.alt02: Business account opening with Brazilian tax authority data and ownership details
banking.alt03: Opened account showing branch, account number, and Pix payment key
banking.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Show banking through customer actions: opening individual and business accounts, checking balances, exporting statements, and making Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) payments by key or QR code. Business onboarding includes documents, owners, and representatives. The institution's brand and domain identify its offering. Journeys extend to desktop with a consistent experience and light and dark themes. The larger screen supports document review; mobile supports access on the go. Explain channel coverage by showing the corresponding screens and the same banking relationship across devices.
credito-app.alt01: Item-based loan simulation showing the rate and estimated amount
credito-app.alt02: Approved offer showing total effective cost (CET) and terms
credito-app.alt03: Accepted transaction with tracking and records
credito-app.text03: The app builds the credit application around your catalog: supporting documents, simulation, offer, agreement, selfie-based acceptance, and tracking. Catalog configuration shapes the product experience.
credito-app.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain the app as an experience guided by the credit platform's catalog. Customers submit supporting documents, simulate terms, review the offer and agreement, accept with a selfie, and track active applications. To explain how an offering appears in the channel, show that the app presents the information and steps supplied by the platform. For receivables, the generic channel manages this communication through an API. The institution configures the product and retains its brand identity, while customers see clear terms and actions throughout application and tracking.
agro.alt01: Illustrative scene: farmer walking through a field with cattle at sunset
agro.text03: Farmers access credit backed by their herd. The institution monitors animal health and transaction obligations through an offering that can carry your brand.
agro.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Start with the farmer and the living assets behind the loan. The herd remains active throughout the contract, and its condition is part of collateral monitoring. Garantia Viva brings together origination, decisioning, contracting, tracking, animal health, liens, covenants, and agreements. Explain the distinctive agricultural workflow through this ongoing view of the assets and associated obligations. The relationship carries the institution's brand, while the instrument documents the credit and the team maintains visibility into the transaction and the farmer's commitments.
imovel.alt01: Illustrative scene: female executive outside a modernist home with a pool
imovel.text03: Customers access loans secured by real estate. The institution reviews the property registry record, appraisal, certificates, and lien priority to guide underwriting and contracting.
imovel.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Present real estate as an asset that supports a loan. The credit desk handles simulation, underwriting, and contracting, while the collateral domain organizes the property registry record, appraisal, certificates, and liens in registration order. Identify the product as a home equity loan secured by real estate. The offer presents terms and a payment schedule; the team reviews the documentation and property context. This combination meets the customer's credit needs while keeping collateral linked to the transaction throughout the contract.
auto.alt01: Illustrative scene: executive beside an unbranded sedan
auto.text02: Auto · put your plans in motion.
auto.text03: Vehicle-secured lending managed by the credit desk: simulation, underwriting, instrument, collateral, disbursement through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), and installment generation.
auto.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Introduce vehicle-secured lending through the customer's needs. Desk-assisted contracting brings together terms, decisioning, the instrument, collateral creation, and disbursement through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), with installments for ongoing servicing. Explain that the team manages contracting through the web assistant and credit desk, supported by the platform's calculation, decisioning, and documentation capabilities. Customers receive clear terms and support from a team with the context to manage the loan; the institution adds the offering to its portfolio and distribution.
consorcio.alt01: Illustrative scene: group gathered in a circular travertine plaza
consorcio.text01: Flagship offering · consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group)
consorcio.text03: Participants choose a group, simulate their purchase credit, and enroll. Conversations explain group meetings, draws, bids, credit allocation, and the documents needed to release purchase credit, with ongoing support.
consorcio.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Introduce consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group) as a group-based planned purchase arrangement. The institution provides simulations, guidance, enrollment, and membership support through agents equipped with tools and a knowledge base. Agents qualify inquiries, check groups, run simulations, record enrollment, report membership status, and support representatives. Participants receive guidance on meetings, draws, and bids within the process managed by the group administrator. Explain the product through planned purchasing: participants build purchase credit with the group and receive allocation through a draw or bid, according to the group's rules.
produtos-panorama.text04: One portfolio. Multiple ways to operate.
produtos-panorama.text08: Personal · payroll-deductible loan · vehicle · home equity
produtos-panorama.text12: CCB (bank credit note) · loan agreement · commercial note · debenture
produtos-panorama.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. For executives, organize the portfolio into three families: liquidity, installment credit, and asset-backed borrowing. Close with planned purchasing. Each has concrete requirements: assignor and debtor for assignments; income and schedules for personal loans; deduction capacity and payroll registration for payroll-deductible loans; assets and liens for secured lending; crop cycles and herd condition for agricultural credit; issuance and units for series. Products and legal instruments serve different roles: CCB (bank credit note), loan agreements, commercial notes, and debentures document transactions according to their nature and policy. Consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group) follows its own planned purchase cycle.
recebiveis.text02: A clear path for every receivable.
recebiveis.text03: Individuals or businesses assign receivables, with distinct roles for assignor and debtor. Assignment, settlement account controls, and checks before disbursement connect the offer, collateral, and net proceeds paid through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system).
recebiveis.alt01: Credit desk transactions showing disbursement status
recebiveis.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. The assignor transfers the right to payment; the debtor owes the receivable. Underwriting considers the instrument and its counterparties; the discount and charges flow into the offer and assignment agreement. Settlement account controls direct the payer's future inflows to the transaction and must be activated before disbursement. Immediately before the Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) transfer, the platform rechecks balances, confirms single use of the note and transfer, recalculates amounts, and links collateral atomically. It then tracks incoming payments. The team verifies the signature, sealed PDF, and completion certificate.
credito-pessoal.alt01: Approved personal loan simulation with Price amortization, total effective cost (CET), IOF (financial transactions tax), and payment schedule
credito-pessoal.text02: Personal loans · terms that fit the plan.
credito-pessoal.text03: Offer personal loans with Price, SAC, or BULLET amortization, a payment schedule, and total effective cost (CET). The credit desk simulates, decides, completes execution, disburses through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), and tracks installments.
credito-pessoal.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. The buyer configures the product and its policy; the borrower sees the amount, terms, and due dates. Price provides a level scheduled payment; SAC uses constant principal amortization with declining payments; BULLET pays periodic interest and concentrates principal at final maturity in the calculation engine. A CCB (bank credit note) or loan agreement documents the transaction according to policy. The credit desk and web contracting assistant manage this installment lending journey.
credito-consignado.text03: CLT private-sector employees, INSS benefit recipients, and employer agreements each have specific rules. Agreement terms, available deduction capacity, and payroll registration guide contracting; batch remittances identify each contract and settle its corresponding installment.
credito-consignado.text06: Specific rules for CLT employees, INSS recipients, and employer agreements.
credito-consignado.text12: Identify the contract and settle the installment.
credito-consignado.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Start with employment or benefit eligibility and available payroll deduction capacity. Operations register the employer agreement, calculate deduction capacity, record payroll authorization, and maintain the link to installments. Batch remittances are reconciled line by line; employee or benefit identifiers and contract numbers distinguish transactions for the same CPF, Brazil's individual taxpayer ID. Rules for CLT private-sector employees and INSS benefit recipients are configured for each regime. The institution manages integration with the selected regime's systems. The law covering CLT payroll-deductible loans appears on the corresponding regulatory slide.
credito-veiculo.text02: Vehicle lending · manage the asset's full cycle.
credito-veiculo.text03: Identification and appraisal support vehicle valuation. The credit desk tracks lien creation, filing, and release, with lending limits, deadlines, and evidence linked to the transaction.
credito-veiculo.alt01: Documents for a vehicle-secured loan application
credito-veiculo.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. The asset record includes identification, valuation, appraisal, and existing encumbrances. Policy uses the lending limit and asset condition, with disbursement tied to lien creation. The team records the filing reference, monitors deadlines, and retains release evidence. SNG/B3 provides the external vehicle lien infrastructure; the platform organizes records and desk workflows, while the institution accesses that infrastructure through its registration partner.
credito-imovel.text02: Home equity · the property record anchors the collateral.
credito-imovel.text03: Home equity brings together real estate collateral, an appraisal, certificates, and lending capacity for each property record. Lien priority guides underwriting; payoff and release documents complete the collateral cycle.
credito-imovel.alt01: Home equity simulation with appraisal, certificates, and liens
credito-imovel.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Present the product as a loan secured by real estate, also known as home equity. The property registry record identifies the asset; lending capacity reflects valuation and liens in registration order. Disbursement follows registration, and the desk manages filing references and deadlines. At payoff, the platform issues the document supporting collateral cancellation at the competent registry, where the release is recorded.
credito-rural.text04: Crop cycle, acreage, production, and coverage inform agricultural lending policy. The CPR (rural product note) documents the commitment; schedules, registration, and monitoring connect contracting to the farmer's production cycle.
credito-rural.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain the agricultural credit product and its CPR (rural product note) instrument. The CPR represents a promise to deliver agricultural products and allows financial settlement under the applicable legal conditions. The agricultural credit offering combines crop data, coverage, decisioning, and CPR issuance and registration. The institution selects its credit lines and configures each one. The next slide explores livestock collateral; the legal reference appears on the collateral regulation slide.
rebanho.text02: Living collateral calls for ongoing insight.
rebanho.text03: Animal health, tracking, and obligations inform herd monitoring. The team manages the transaction through covenants and agreements linked to the loan.
rebanho.alt01: Livestock credit offers and an accepted transaction
rebanho.alt02: Herd health form within the offer
rebanho.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Move from the farm scene to the team's daily work. The transaction record brings the loan and pledged herd into view; health and tracking data add context for collateral monitoring. Covenants and agreements organize obligations throughout the relationship. Explain that Garantia Viva supports ongoing monitoring and management of the agricultural transaction after contracting. The team reviews animal condition and contractual commitments to guide action, keeping the farmer, collateral, and credit in the same context. Animal identification, health, tracking, liens, covenants, and agreements provide a continuous view of living collateral.
credito-series.text02: Commercial notes and debentures · issued by series.
credito-series.text03: Structure transactions by series, unit face value, and units. Issuance, signing, registration, and payment allocation keep each series, holding, and receipt connected.
credito-series.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Present a commercial note as a corporate debt instrument and a debenture as debt issued by a corporation, subject to each instrument's requirements. The platform organizes series, unit face value, units, and allocation; policy identifies applicable providers, such as the registrar and fiduciary agent. Payments for a series are distributed across its units. The depository interface records filing references and registration status. Distribution and deposit are handled by the institution's selected providers.
credito-mutuo-ccb.text01: Loan agreements and CCB (bank credit note)
credito-mutuo-ccb.text02: Loan agreements and CCB · terms become a contract.
credito-mutuo-ccb.text03: The offer sets the amount, rate, installments, and obligations. Loan agreements and CCB document the transaction according to its nature and policy, with an identified document, signature, and ongoing monitoring.
credito-mutuo-ccb.text07: Selected by transaction type and policy.
credito-mutuo-ccb.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explain the credit offering and its legal form. A loan agreement documents the lending arrangement; a CCB (bank credit note) records the promise to pay in the appropriate banking transaction. The instrument catalog supports selection of the applicable form within the product, guided by the institution's legal review. Document assembly, numbering, hash, and signature retain the link to the offer and transaction. The same foundation calculates installments and tracks payments.
produto-consorcio.text07: Consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group) · from enrollment to purchase credit.
produto-consorcio.text08: The relationship starts with the group and enrollment. Conversations explain meetings, draws, bids, and credit allocation; membership status and documents guide support through the release of purchase credit.
produto-consorcio.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Present consórcio (Brazilian pooled purchase group) as planned purchasing alongside the credit products. Agents check groups and terms, run simulations, record enrollment, and review membership status, including requirements for releasing purchase credit. The knowledge base guides participants through meetings, draws, and bids. The administrator manages the group and its meetings; the platform supports service, sales, and membership tracking.
pacote-produto.text02: Your product arrives as a complete package.
pacote-produto.text03: An installable vertical brings products, policy, workflows, contracts, the fund account, and app keys into one package. Installation configures the offering automatically.
pacote-produto.text08: FUND ACCOUNT · APP KEYS · AUTOMATED CONFIGURATION
pacote-produto.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. The installable vertical organizes products, policy, workflows, contracts, the fund account, and app keys, with an owner for each outstanding requirement. For installment credit, the package combines simulation, Decision, the instrument, collateral, disbursement through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), and installments. Personal, payroll-deductible, vehicle, home equity, and agricultural loans retain their own data on the shared foundation. The institution selects the offering and parameters; installation assembles the package within its organization.
proposta.alt01: Approved offer with amount, discount, total effective cost (CET), and receiving account
proposta.alt02: Readable transaction agreement in the app
proposta.text02: The value is clear to your customer.
proposta.text03: Discount, interest rate, IOF (financial transactions tax), total effective cost (CET), and payment schedule come together in the offer. Customers review the terms, choose to accept, and track the application in the app.
proposta.text04: DISCOUNT · RATE · IOF · CET · PAYMENT SCHEDULE
proposta.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Read the offer from the customer's perspective. The discount, interest rate, IOF (financial transactions tax), total effective cost (CET), and payment schedule explain net proceeds, borrowing costs, and the timing of payments. The calculator supports Price, SAC, and BULLET according to the product. Show the offer details and the in-app application journey to demonstrate how customers review terms before acceptance. Acceptance records agreement with the terms; execution brings together an email invitation, code confirmation, and a signed document, with clear responsibilities at each step.
parametros.text03: Product, risk bands, and policy determine rates, terms, instruments, and operating conditions. Each offering follows the institution's rules and minimum thresholds.
parametros.alt01: Simulation with lending capacity, risk band, total effective cost (CET), IOF (financial transactions tax), and a Price payment schedule
parametros.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Policy establishes defaults and minimum thresholds; the product defines its terms and risk bands. Published configuration informs the offer, decision, and document. The financial engine handles calculations, covered in a dedicated chapter.
calculo-sistemas.text02: A payment schedule that follows cash flow.
calculo-sistemas.text03: Price, SAC, and BULLET; an initial interest-only period; balloon payments; stepped installments; custom schedules. Choose the amortization structure that fits the transaction.
calculo-sistemas.text11: Same loan · R$10,000.00 · 1% per month · 6 months · common scale, 4 px minimum
calculo-sistemas.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Price: level payments. SAC: constant principal amortization and declining payments. BULLET: periodic interest with all principal due in the final installment. Initial interest-only period: the customer pays interest during the grace period, followed by Price or SAC amortization. Balloon: a portion of principal is reserved for the end. Stepped: installments increase in stages. Custom: the institution defines the schedule. The bars show the same R$10,000.00 loan at 1% per month over six months, on a common scale; small installments have a minimum height of 4 px for visibility.
calculo-comparacao.text02: The same loan with Price, SAC, and BULLET.
calculo-comparacao.text03: R$10,000.00 · 1% PER MONTH · 3 MONTHS · CALCULATED, ILLUSTRATIVE AMOUNTS
calculo-comparacao.text40: Price spreads principal repayment; SAC reduces each payment; BULLET holds principal until final maturity. Bars share a common scale in Brazilian reais, with a 4 px minimum for visibility.
calculo-comparacao.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Illustrative figures explain the amortization methods. Presentation convention: round interest to cents each month and adjust the final installment to bring the balance to zero. Price: A = P × i / [1 − (1 + i)^−n]; before rounding, A = 3,400.2211148…; payments are 3,400.22 / 3,400.22 / 3,400.23; interest is 100.00 / 67.00 / 33.67. SAC: principal amortization of 3,333.33 / 3,333.33 / 3,333.34 and interest of 100.00 / 66.67 / 33.33. BULLET: interest of 100.00 each month and principal of 10,000.00 in the third installment. In all three methods, total payments equal principal plus interest, and the ending balance is zero. The engine retains internal precision beyond cents; the table illustrates the presentation convention and final adjustment. Bars share a common scale, with a 4 px minimum height for visibility.
calculo-operacao.text02: From the rate to the funds received.
calculo-operacao.text03: Interest, IOF (financial transactions tax), fees, and dates determine transaction cost. In receivables financing, the discount and other deductions determine net proceeds; total effective cost (CET) reflects the customer's full payment stream.
calculo-operacao.text04: CET 2.40% PER MONTH · SHOWN IN THE OFFER
calculo-operacao.text05: Platform screen · Portuguese UI · fictitious data
calculo-operacao.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Distinguish principal, net proceeds, and total payments. A financed fee increases the financed amount; a deducted fee reduces net proceeds. Scheduled or recurring borrower fees appear on the correct dates in the cash flow used to calculate total effective cost (CET); institution-borne costs remain with the institution. For receivables financing, start with face value, apply adjustments to the underlying receivables and the discount, deduct applicable charges, and show net proceeds paid through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system). CET relates net proceeds to payments and their due dates: it is a rate for the entire cash flow.
calculo-reuso.text02: The simulation carries through to the contract.
calculo-reuso.text03: One financial engine serves your credit products. With the same data, dates, and version of terms, the simulation, offer, payment schedule, and contract show the same figures.
calculo-reuso.text08: SAME DATA · SAME DATES · SAME VERSION OF TERMS
calculo-reuso.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain reuse through the financial capabilities: receivables discounting, IOF (financial transactions tax), total effective cost (CET), and amortization methods. Each product uses its own formula: receivables financing uses a discount calculation, while installment credit uses its payment schedule. Figures remain consistent because the simulation, offer, schedule, and contract use the same product, published terms, dates, fees, and rounding convention. When an input changes, the platform recalculates the simulation and updates the offer.
precificacao.text02: Rates shaped by product and policy.
precificacao.text03: Product rates, risk bands, and institution rules define pricing. The published version, effective period, and terms feed into the simulation and offer.
precificacao.text11: VERSION · EFFECTIVE PERIOD · PUBLISHED TERMS → SIMULATION AND OFFER
precificacao.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Policy sets the defaults; products and risk bands define specific offering terms within the established minimums. Operations apply the published version. Fee rules add effective periods, priority, and amount and term ranges. The AI assistant consults published parameters and calculations; pricing always comes from the institution's policy.
tarifas.text02: Every fee has a rule and a payer.
tarifas.text03: Origination and onboarding fees have defined amounts, application rules, and payers for each product. Effective periods and ranges govern application; scheduled workflows support recurring charges.
tarifas.alt01: Scheduled product fees with amount ranges, effective periods, and versions
tarifas.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Fee rules support fixed and percentage amounts, limits, financing, and cost allocation. Scheduled rules select by effective period, priority, and range. Recurring collection combines a scheduled workflow trigger with billing on the due date. Show the buyer how each fee is structured. Onboarding and origination are pricing categories; the institution chooses which apply to each product under the rules for its segment.
custos-proposta.text02:
Your customer sees
the full cost
of borrowing.
custos-proposta.text03: The offer separates interest, IOF (financial transactions tax), fees, installments, and net proceeds. Total effective cost (CET) includes borrower charges; partner commissions have their own records and designated payer.
custos-proposta.text14: CET · BORROWER CHARGES · DEDICATED PARTNER COMMISSION RECORDS
custos-proposta.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. The offer shows deductions, financed charges, and future payments. Each rule identifies the payer and whether the charge is included in total effective cost (CET); institution-borne costs remain with the institution. Commercial rules define who pays partner commissions, subject to the institution's review. The simulation and offer retain the rule and its version so the team can verify what was applied.
parceiros-comissoes.text03: Partners and banking correspondents have profiles and product-specific rules. Each application identifies its channel; commissions are calculated per transaction, and the portal shows originations, statements, and payouts at disbursement.
parceiros-comissoes.alt01: Partner setup with per-transaction compensation rules
parceiros-comissoes.alt02: Simulation showing the originating partner and transaction commission
parceiros-comissoes.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Registration enables the partner and its products; each application retains its originating channel and partner. Both inform decisioning, including for installment products. The rule determines the expected commission; disbursement triggers its recording and payment through the payout interface. The partner portal supports link-based origination, rule review, and commission statements. Operations maintain batches and reversals, with each payout executed once.
instrumentos.text10:
CCB, loan agreements, and assignments ·
give every transaction its form.
instrumentos.text11: A CCB documents bank debt; a loan agreement sets out the loan; an assignment agreement transfers the receivable. The platform assembles and numbers the PDF, stores its hash, routes it for signing, and records execution.
instrumentos.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. A CCB (bank credit note) links the promise to pay to the banking transaction; a loan agreement sets out the loan and its terms; an assignment agreement identifies the transferred rights, assignor, and assignee. For each, policy selects the applicable instrument. The platform assembles it from the offer, assigns a number, and stores the PDF and SHA-256 hash. The signing service returns a sealed PDF and completion certificate; the execution record retains evidence and the transaction link. Opening a linked assignment transaction requires a verified signature. Internal execution records and external registration serve distinct purposes: submit the instrument to the competent registry when required by its nature, retaining its filing reference and confirmation.
instrumento-cpr.text03: The CPR documents the agricultural commitment. Production details, maturity, and collateral form the numbered PDF; its hash, signature, and registration reference keep it linked to the transaction.
instrumento-cpr.text12: Registration reference linked to the transaction.
instrumento-cpr.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Purpose: the CPR (rural product note) records an agricultural commitment, with physical delivery or financial settlement under applicable law. Assembly: the instrument receives parties, subject matter, due dates, and pledged assets from the product data. The platform assigns a number, stores the PDF and hash, and routes it for signing; the sealed PDF and completion certificate become part of the execution record. Issuance starts registration deadline tracking, and the external interface captures the filing reference and response. Registration or deposit requirements are set out in Lei nº 8.929 (Brazilian rural product note law), August 22, 1994, article 12, as amended: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/leis/l8929.htm.
instrumentos-series.text07: Commercial notes and debentures organize corporate debt by series and units. The platform assembles and numbers each document and stores its hash; signing and registration connect the instrument, series, and payments.
instrumentos-series.text08: Assemble, number, and store the hash
instrumentos-series.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Purpose: commercial notes represent corporate debt; debentures document debt issued by corporations, with their own requirements and service providers. For both, policy defines the instrument and series, with unit face value and units; assembly produces a PDF identified by number and hash. Signing retains the sealed PDF and certificate; the execution record stores the evidence. The depository interface retains the request, filing reference, and confirmation; payments are allocated to units. The institution selects the depository and issuance structure.
registros-baixas.text02: Registration and release each have a purpose.
registros-baixas.text03: Execution, liens, and adverse credit records each have dedicated records. The desk tracks filing references, deadlines, and evidence: from vehicle liens to property payoff documents and removal of adverse records after an agreement.
registros-baixas.text12: Filing and removal after an agreement
registros-baixas.text13: REGISTRATION ≠ RELEASE · FILING REFERENCE · DEADLINE · EVIDENCE
registros-baixas.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain three distinct acts. Instrument: issuance, signing, retention of execution evidence, and applicable external registration. Collateral: creation and release of vehicle liens through SNG/B3, and real estate registration with payoff documentation supporting cancellation. Adverse credit records: filing and removal after an agreement. Each act retains evidence, an owner, and its link to the transaction; release or removal is confirmed by the competent external authority.
fluxo.text02: A clear next step at every stage.
fluxo.text03: Triggers, dependencies, and response waits organize recurring work. The team handles review and authorization wherever its input is required.
fluxo.text11: The team reviews and authorizes at defined steps.
fluxo.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Show how work recurring across contracts is organized. The workflow engine combines triggers, dependencies, and response waits to connect credit, communication, payments, decisioning, and AI activities. The desk brings together human review and authorization. Explain cross-team coordination through workflows that sequence activities and resume work on expected events and responses. The institution configures its operations with these capabilities, keeping the customer, contract, and team responsibilities at the center.
medir-valor.text05: Every contract brings together three dimensions of value: clarity for customers, organized work for the team, and evidence that explains the transaction.
medir-valor.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Give leadership a business-centered unit of value: the contract. The offer details customer terms; the desk brings together execution records and operational actions; policy and audit trails provide records for reviewing the journey. Explain institutional value through these three capabilities within one journey. They support assessment of completed work and information available at each handoff. The economic discussion starts with the institution's process and platform usage, using customer experience, operations, and governance as concrete reference points.
politica.text03: Decision is the shared engine across all credit products. Define policies in DMN, connect data sources, and govern decisions with version control and traceability.
politica.alt01: Personal loan policy decision table with versions and publishing
politica.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Put policy ownership at the center of the product. Decision is the shared engine across credit products, organizing rules in DMN and versioned tables with connected external sources. Explain that the institution defines its criteria and monitors their application. The same foundation supports different offerings while retaining product-specific requirements. This chapter covers modeling, simulation, publishing without an application deployment, traces, and asynchronous execution; the desk adds approval authority, dual approval, and AI that prepares decisions for human confirmation.
versoes.text02: Every policy version stays on record.
versoes.text03: The team models rules and retains their versions. Decision traces show the criteria applied and sources consulted.
versoes.text09: The trace shows each decision's criteria and sources.
versoes.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explore the work of maintaining credit policy. The risk team expresses its criteria in DMN and decision tables, retaining versions to track rule changes. Each execution trace shows the criteria applied and sources consulted. To explain which rule governed a case, show the versioned policy and execution trace. This gives the institution a shared reference for reviewing decisions and updating products, keeping the rules closely connected to business accountability.
fontes-decisao.text03: Connected external sources feed the Decision pipeline. The team models dependencies and uses the trace to review the information used in each execution.
fontes-decisao.alt01: External data sources by decision pipeline, with failure-handling policy
fontes-decisao.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Present decisioning as the combination of criteria and information. Decision connects external sources to the pipeline and applies DMN policy, preserving the path in the trace. Explain how data informs assessment by showing the sources linked to policy and their role in execution. The institution defines which information matters for its product and reviews the path to the outcome. When a bureau inquiry calls for human input, the application goes to the desk so the team can continue the assessment.
politica-ciclo.text03: Write, version, and simulate your policy before publishing. Publish directly to the shared credit engine, independently of application deployments.
politica-ciclo.text08: SIMULATE BEFORE PUBLISHING · PUBLISH INDEPENDENTLY OF APPLICATION DEPLOYMENTS
politica-ciclo.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Walk through policy maintenance from the risk team's perspective. The team writes a change in DMN, retains the version, and runs a simulation against reference cases to review outcomes. It then publishes the policy independently of application deployment. Explain that rule changes are published within Decision. Credit products use this shared engine, while the institution owns the criteria, evaluates simulation results, and selects the published version.
porque-decisao.alt01: Working capital decision requirements covering identity risk, repayment capacity, and coverage
porque-decisao.text02: See the path behind every decision.
porque-decisao.text03: Each execution trace brings together the sources consulted, the policy applied, and the steps leading to the outcome. The team reviews the decision with its full context.
porque-decisao.alt02: Rule inputs showing the source of each field
porque-decisao.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Open a Decision execution and walk through it with the audience. Start with the sources used, move to the policy, and follow the steps recorded in the trace. Explain an outcome through the elements of that execution: inputs, rule, and path. This record supports risk, operations, and case review across credit products. The policy version and execution path ground discussion of a specific case in the information consulted and the institution's criteria.
decisao-assincrona.text03: Asynchronous execution lets you start an assessment and track its completion. The trace retains each execution path so operations can review the outcome.
decisao-assincrona.text06: The assessment starts with the workflow.
decisao-assincrona.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explain asynchronous execution through the work of starting an assessment and tracking its completion. Decision receives the execution request, processes the policy and its sources, and makes the result available with a trace. To show how multistep decisions are tracked, use the execution identifier and recorded path. Workflows organize triggers, dependencies, and response waits to maintain operational continuity. This shared foundation serves credit products and lets the team review each decision alongside the policy and information used in the assessment.
fila.text02: The credit desk brings the work together.
fila.text03: Cases requiring human review reach the desk with a queue, context, and authority-based decisioning. The team validates eligibility, approves, verifies execution documents, and authorizes disbursement.
fila.alt01: Credit desk with a transaction queue and status for each case
fila.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Show the desk as the team's workspace for daily credit operations. Cases requiring human review enter the queue; the team reviews context, acts within its authority, and records a decision so the workflow can continue. Eligibility, execution documentation, approval, and authorization organize the operational steps. Open the queue and a case to show where analysts work. This view brings together responsibility, information, and the next action, with a second person for cases requiring dual approval.
dossie.text03: The case file puts review in context.
dossie.text04: At the desk, the signed agreement, sealed PDF, and completion certificate bring execution documents together for review. The team checks these documents as it manages the transaction.
dossie.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Present the case file through the review process. The team finds the signed agreement, sealed PDF, and completion certificate linked to transaction execution. Show these documents and the case identifier to explain what analysts review. The trace adds visibility into the policy applied, while the AI assistant reads the queue, case file, and fund balance to prepare the decision. The team uses this context to conduct its assessment and record its actions.
alcada.text02: Every decision has a defined authority.
alcada.text03: Approval authority determines who can decide. Cases above the assigned limit receive a second person's approval; the desk decision returns to the workflow under dual control.
alcada.alt01: Desk case awaiting second approval for a decision above the assigned authority limit
alcada.alt02: Queue requiring a second person for every decision
alcada.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Policy defines desk routing and decision authority. Above the assigned limit, a second person approves; the decision returns to the workflow under dual control. When policy calls for human judgment, the application reaches the desk with its full context. The queue, case file, and records link the analyst's decision to the next operational step. Show routing and assigned responsibility to explain who decides special cases.
pendencias.text02: Every follow-up has a clear destination.
pendencias.text03: The team identifies documents that need additional information and tracks the request. Submitted documents feed data extraction and the workflow; customers follow progress in the app or portal.
pendencias.text05: The team identifies the additional information needed.
pendencias.text09: Customers track progress in the app or portal.
pendencias.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Use a supporting document requiring review as the example. The team checks the application and received documents; extraction turns document fields into workflow data, while application tracking keeps the customer informed. Explain visibility through the desk and customer channels: app and portal. The operational value comes from continuity between incoming information, assessment, and the next action, with documents and data supporting transaction management.
ia-mesa.text03: The assistant reads the queue, case file, and fund balance, prepares the decision, and presents the context. A person confirms the decision before it is recorded at the desk.
ia-mesa.alt01: Review queue beside the assistant: a person confirms approval and checks the fund balance
ia-mesa.text05: Read the queue and fund balance.
ia-mesa.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Present AI as support for the desk team. The assistant reads the queue, consults the case file, and considers the fund balance to prepare the decision. A person reviews the context and confirms the record. Explain accountability through human confirmation and the institution's approval authority governance. Decision remains the shared policy engine; the assistant prepares the team's next action. This division makes the role of rules, the contribution of AI, and the case owner's responsibility explicit.
garantias-mesa.text04: Before disbursement, the platform rechecks balances, verifies note and transfer usage, recalculates amounts, and links collateral atomically. Releasing held collateral requires dual approval.
garantias-mesa.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Show the control applied immediately before funds are released. The platform rechecks the settlement record balance, confirms single use of the note and transfer, recalculates amounts, and links collateral atomically. Explain collateral verification through this check before disbursement. Releasing held collateral requires dual approval. This complements verification of the signed assignment and authorization of Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), giving the desk clear actions for documents, collateral, and disbursement.
aceite-cliente.text03: Through a link or portal, customers review total effective cost (CET), IOF (financial transactions tax), and installments, confirm their CPF taxpayer ID, and accept the offer. A hash and source identify the acceptance record.
aceite-cliente.text04: CET · IOF · INSTALLMENTS · CPF · HASH · SOURCE
aceite-cliente.alt01: Marked transaction agreement and selfie-based acceptance
aceite-cliente.text11: Platform screen · Portuguese UI · fictitious data
aceite-cliente.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Show the customer's role in accepting a desk-issued offer. The link or portal presents total effective cost (CET), IOF (financial transactions tax), and installments for review; the customer confirms their CPF taxpayer ID and accepts the terms. A hash and source identify the record. Use acceptance and its identifiers to link the offer to the customer's agreement. The contract then proceeds to electronic signing, with a sealed PDF and completion certificate. This sequence supports understanding of the terms and gives clear roles to offer acceptance and execution of the governing instrument.
formalizacao.text04: The customer receives an email invitation, verifies with a code, and signs. A sealed PDF and completion certificate support review; for a linked assignment, the server verifies the signature before opening the transaction.
formalizacao.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain execution through what each participant receives. The signatory opens the email invitation, verifies with a six-digit code, and signs. The team reviews the sealed PDF and completion certificate. Use the signature, PDF, and certificate to show how the contract is identified and verifiable. For an assignment with linked counterparties, the server verifies the signature before opening the transaction. This step connects the customer's agreement to continued contracting and desk operations.
desembolso.text03: Transaction review and payment authorization each serve a specific purpose. Payment is confirmed upon settlement through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), with authorization controls ensuring a single debit.
desembolso.text11: Authorization controls ensure a single debit.
desembolso.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain the team's distinct transaction actions. Review provides context for assessment; approval records the operational decision; authorization starts the release of funds. Payment is confirmed upon settlement through Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), and repeat controls ensure one debit even with concurrent authorizations. Explain release tracking through authorization and settlement confirmation as identifiable moments. The desk manages authorization, while transactional controls manage disbursement execution, keeping human action and financial effect clear.
console.text02: Every role has a clear workspace.
console.text03: The console brings together accounts, holds, applications, and role-based access with two-factor authentication. A second approval governs actions requiring another person.
console.alt01: Console with account openings under human review, showing reasons and comparisons
console.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Show the back office through the start of a working day. Each operator enters the console according to their role, with two-factor authentication, and reviews accounts, holds, applications, and access. Actions requiring a second approval involve another person. Explain work allocation through roles, access controls, and approvals. The console gives the institution an operational view of customer relationships, while the desk brings together credit actions. The team works with defined responsibilities and information relevant to each role.
documentos-fluxos.text05: Extraction turns document fields into workflow data. Triggers, dependencies, and response waits coordinate execution across 222 action types.
documentos-fluxos.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Introduce automation through a familiar task: receiving a document and using its fields in operations. Extraction reads the file and supplies data to a workflow, which organizes triggers, dependencies, and response waits. Explain workflow scope through the catalog's 222 action types, including credit, decisioning, AI, WhatsApp, Pix (Brazil's instant payment system), and boleto, a Brazilian payment slip. The count conveys the engine's breadth; keep the focus on the document and the work it enables in the journey. Group extraction, financial actions, communication, and AI into workflows with triggers, dependencies, and response waits. Extraction supplies fields to the workflow; review and decisioning each have their own steps.
conversa.alt01: Illustrative scene: manager in a travertine setting with the carved catalisa logo
conversa.text03: The official WhatsApp channel connects service and operations. Multilingual agents use tools selected by the institution; transactional email delivers invitations and codes, while workflows carry each interaction forward.
conversa.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Explain agents through the service they provide to customers and teams. The institution selects instructions and tools, and agents respond in the contact's language, including through the official WhatsApp channel using Meta's Cloud API. Transactional email delivers invitations, codes, and notices, with DKIM and SPF. Explain AI's role through guidance, service, and use of the tools selected for each agent. Workflows connect communication to the next action. In credit review, the assistant prepares the decision and a person confirms the record, as shown on the desk AI slide; Decision applies policy.
portais.alt01: Customer portal with active transactions, series, and due dates
portais.text02: Customers stay informed through a link.
portais.text03: The customer portal brings together transactions, installments, documents, and applications. Link-based access connects the institution with borrowers and provides decision explanations and a review channel.
portais.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Borrowers follow a link to review their transactions, installments, documents, and applications. The relationship continues beyond the offer: the team keeps tracking information in one accessible place. Link expiration and access conditions are part of channel configuration and security. Correspondent distribution and partner statements are covered on the partners and commissions slide.
boleto.text02: Connect each payment to its installment.
boleto.text03: The desk issues the boleto, the customer receives the PDF, and payment reconciliation settles the installment. The team tracks receipts within the transaction.
boleto.text05: The desk issues it; the customer receives the PDF.
boleto.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Present collections through the lifecycle of an installment. The desk issues a boleto (Brazilian payment slip), the customer receives the PDF, and payment is reconciled to settle the corresponding installment. Explain payment recognition through the link between the billing document, reconciled payment, and installment settlement. Tracking stays within the credit transaction so the team can follow the contract. This connects routine receipts to monitoring and collections managed by the institution's team.
regua-cobranca.text02: Let the portfolio guide the conversation.
regua-cobranca.text03: Monitoring after disbursement brings together active transactions and early warning indicators. Policy-based outreach tells the team whom to contact each day.
regua-cobranca.alt01: Monitoring after disbursement with current and past-due transactions and alerts
regua-cobranca.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Present the outreach strategy as a working tool. The desk monitors active transactions, flags early warning indicators, and checks whom to contact under policy. Explain next-action selection through monitoring and the outreach strategy. The institution organizes its work around portfolio context and relationship criteria. Contact becomes part of ongoing credit servicing alongside installments, receipts, and contractual commitments, giving focus to the collections team's daily work.
renegociacao.text05: An agreement keeps the relationship moving.
renegociacao.text06: The desk manages restructuring agreements, monitors covenants, and files or removes adverse credit records. Transaction context remains available throughout servicing.
renegociacao.text08: Adverse credit records filed or removed
renegociacao.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Present restructuring as continuity in the borrower relationship. The desk concludes agreements, monitors covenants, and files or removes adverse credit records while retaining transaction data. Explain changes to terms through the agreement and tracking of associated commitments. The team keeps the transaction context as it explores repayment arrangements. This connects to monitoring after disbursement and outreach, allowing the institution to manage collections, contractual commitments, and relationships across the same portfolio.
trava-recebiveis.text03: Receivables settlement controls link the payer's future inflows to the transaction and direct them to the fund. Disbursement requires active controls.
trava-recebiveis.text10: ACTIVE SETTLEMENT CONTROLS REQUIRED FOR DISBURSEMENT
trava-recebiveis.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explain settlement controls as the link between receivables flows and the credit transaction. The payer's future inflows are tied to the transaction and directed to the fund; credit disbursement requires active controls. Show this routing and its link to disbursement to explain how receivables support repayment. The team tracks the transaction with the context of linked inflows, complementing collateral checks and payment authorization. This capability connects lending to the monitoring of its repayment source.
cobranca-link.text03: Connect your gateway and collect by payment link. Payment triggers a workflow, connecting the receipt to the next operational action.
cobranca-link.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Present ad hoc payment collection as a capability the institution offers its own customers. The connected gateway belongs to its operations; the link enables collection, and payment triggers a workflow. Explain continuity through the connection between the payment event and the next configured action. The workflow engine organizes dependencies and activities while the gateway handles receipt. This supports payment-link collection and connects the buyer's commercial relationships to operational work.
carteira.text03: The portfolio brings together installment loans, receivables, and monitoring after disbursement. Active transactions, installments, and early warning indicators guide the team's work.
carteira.alt01: Portfolio showing exposure, upcoming and past-due amounts, and suggested credit loss provisions
carteira.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Shift from a single contract to the institution's portfolio. The portfolio brings together installment loans and receivables transactions, with installments, monitoring, and agreements. Explain ongoing servicing through active transactions, early warning indicators, and credit commitments. Personal, payroll-deductible, vehicle, home equity, and agricultural loans can form the desk-managed portfolio. Work continues through portfolio review and receipt management, connecting the offering to the servicing that sustains customer relationships.
provisao-scr.alt01: Portfolio with provisions by stage, period closing, and an SCR 3040 preview for Brazil's credit information system
provisao-scr.text02: A clear view of every reporting period.
provisao-scr.text03: Stage-based provisions and period closing support accounting under Resolução CMN nº 4.966 (Brazilian Monetary Council), November 25, 2021. An SCR 3040 preview is available as a CSV for review.
provisao-scr.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explain portfolio accounting through the closing process. The platform calculates stage-based provisions to support accounting under Resolução CMN nº 4.966 (Brazilian Monetary Council), November 25, 2021, closes the reporting period, and generates a CSV preview of SCR 3040, Brazil's credit information report, for the accountant. Show the provision and preview as the accounting team's review materials. The institution manages validation and submission to the BCB, Brazil's central bank. Source: Resolução CMN nº 4.966, November 25, 2021. Scope: accounting concepts and criteria for financial instruments and hedge accounting at financial institutions and other BCB-authorized institutions. Relevant provision: stage allocation in article 37. Official BCB text: https://www.bcb.gov.br/estabilidadefinanceira/exibenormativo?numero=4966&tipo=RESOLU%C3%87%C3%83O+CMN.
carteira-garantias.text03: Payroll-deductible loans retain employer agreements, remittances, deduction capacity, and payroll registration. Real estate collateral retains property records and lien priority. Covenants and agreements track each transaction's commitments.
carteira-garantias.text12: COVENANTS AND AGREEMENTS TRACK EVERY TRANSACTION
carteira-garantias.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Show why portfolio servicing retains product-specific information. For payroll-deductible loans, the team records employer agreements and remittances, checks deduction capacity, and registers payroll deductions. For real estate collateral, it tracks property records, appraisals, certificates, and liens in registration order. Use these two domains to show how operations retain the specifics of collateral and the borrower's relationship. Covenants and agreements complete the view of commitments. Shared decisioning and operations serve the portfolio while each product retains the elements needed for its management.
trilha.text02: Every transaction has a recorded history.
trilha.text03: The organization's audit trail records transaction outcomes. Versioned policy and traces retain the decision path; agreements, acceptances, collateral, and audit records use server-signed writes.
trilha.text07: agreements, acceptances, and collateral · signed writes
trilha.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Start with the need to explain a transaction. The audit trail records decision outcomes by organization; Decision retains the policy execution path. Agreements, acceptances, collateral, and audit records use server-signed writes. Explain evidence preservation through these mechanisms and their objects: the transaction, decision, and protected records. The team reviews history in the institution's context, linking it to the case under examination and the responsibilities of those managing the credit.
acessos.text06: A dedicated environment for every institution.
acessos.text07: Each organization's data, keys, and events stay within its own environment. Teams enter the console through role-based access with two-factor authentication; protected collections use server-signed writes.
acessos.text08: Role-based console access with two-factor authentication
acessos.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explain segregation through the institution's environment. Each organization maintains dedicated data, keys, and events; teams enter the console according to their roles and with two-factor authentication. Agreement, acceptance, collateral, and audit collections use server-signed writes. Explain institutional separation and responsibility through organization-level isolation, role assignment, and protected records. These mechanisms organize daily work and access to institutional information, supporting clear responsibilities for administrators, operators, and viewers.
identidade.alt01: Illustrative scene: professional walking through travertine portals
identidade.text03: Onboarding checks CPF taxpayer registration status, facial biometrics, and liveness. Codes delivered through the official WhatsApp channel support onboarding and login; a selfie supports acceptance in the credit journey.
identidade.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. Present identity through actions during access and contracting. Onboarding checks CPF taxpayer registration status; facial biometrics use a moving selfie with live gestures; the official WhatsApp channel delivers onboarding and login codes. Explain identity verification through these checkpoints and the selfie used for credit acceptance. The experience combines registration, liveness, and confirmation at clear moments for the customer, while the institution manages the relationship under its brand and within its operating environment.
logs.text03: Logs retain identifiers useful for support. CPF and CNPJ taxpayer IDs, Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) keys, phone numbers, and email addresses are filtered out of these records.
logs.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Explain log handling through support workflows. The team uses identifiers to examine an event, while CPF and CNPJ taxpayer IDs, Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) keys, phone numbers, and email addresses are filtered from the logs. Explain operational diagnostics through the specific treatment of support identifiers and these personal data categories. This complements the organization-level transaction audit trail and history retention. The institution has references for technical monitoring and operational review, with clearly defined records and handling rules.
protecoes.text03: Destination controls for outbound requests, privilege safeguards, and organization-level isolation structure application security. Protected records use server-signed writes.
protecoes.text09: Dedicated data, keys, and events for each institution.
protecoes.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Describe each protection mechanism and its scope. Destination controls enforce boundaries between outbound requests and internal addresses, privilege safeguards preserve role assignments, and organization-level isolation separates each institution's data, keys, and events. Protected collections use server-signed writes. Explain application security through these mechanisms. Together, they organize access, communication, and record changes, with clear boundaries governing who enters, what they access, and how protected data is written.
memoria.text02: A defined policy for retained history.
memoria.notes: Presentation paths: 60. Product retention is 36 months for execution history and 60 months for credit history, configurable with a 12-month minimum. The institution aligns these settings with its purposes and retention obligations. The audit trail attributes actions to executions and makes their context available for review. The FSB frames traceability around "what triggered the action; what information and tools it accessed; what steps it took; and whether it acted within its permissions". As agent usage scales, retained execution records support oversight beyond live human monitoring. Source: FSB, Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Final report, October 15, 2026. Attribution, visibility, and traceability: report p. 26, PDF p. 30. Discussion of human monitoring at scale: report p. 19, PDF p. 23. These are nonbinding sound practices. Official final report: https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P151026-1.pdf.
reg-evidencias.text03: The audit trail records transaction outcomes by organization. Agreements, acceptances, collateral, and audit records use server-signed writes. The team reviews these records to show regulators and auditors the credit journey.
reg-evidencias.text07: AUDIT TRAIL · SIGNED WRITES · RETENTION PERIODS
reg-evidencias.notes: Presentation paths: 20 · 40 · 60. The institution reconstructs each transaction by organization: policy and version, decision and trace, execution documents, desk actions, disbursement, and servicing. The trail records transaction outcomes; signed writes protect operational records. Auditing links those actions to retained evidence and the responsible person, with permission-based review. The platform supports auditing; the institution manages regulatory classification, required evidence, and accountability. The FSB emphasizes attribution, visibility, and traceability, including records to "attribute actions … to specific agents" and visibility through a "unique identifier" for each agent. As usage scales, consultable records support ongoing oversight. Source: FSB, Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Final report, October 15, 2026. Attribution, visibility, and traceability: report p. 26, PDF p. 30. Human monitoring at scale: report p. 19, PDF p. 23. These are nonbinding sound practices. Official final report: https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P151026-1.pdf.
reg-fechamento.text02: A clear foundation for closing review.
reg-fechamento.text03: Stage-based provisions and period closing support accounting under Resolução CMN nº 4.966 (Brazilian Monetary Council), November 25, 2021. An SCR 3040 CSV preview organizes information for the responsible team's review.
reg-fechamento.text09: CSV for review by the responsible team.
reg-fechamento.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. The portfolio calculates stage-based provisions and closes the reporting period. Resolução CMN nº 4.966 (Brazilian Monetary Council), November 25, 2021, covers financial instrument accounting criteria and stage allocation; the institution defines the methodology and validates classification. For the SCR, Brazil's credit information system, the platform generates a CSV preview of report 3040 for the accountant; the institution manages conversion to the current reporting layout, validation, and submission to the BCB, Brazil's central bank. Layout and instructions: https://www.bcb.gov.br/estabilidadefinanceira/scrdoc3040. Source: Resolução CMN nº 4.966, November 25, 2021. Scope: accounting concepts and criteria for financial instruments and hedge accounting at financial institutions and other BCB-authorized institutions. Relevant provision: stage allocation in article 37. Official BCB text: https://www.bcb.gov.br/estabilidadefinanceira/exibenormativo?numero=4966&tipo=RESOLU%C3%87%C3%83O+CMN.
reg-identificacao.text03: CPF taxpayer registration status, facial biometrics, and liveness support KYC. Electronic signing combines code verification, a sealed PDF, and a completion certificate to retain evidence of the act.
reg-identificacao.text06: SOURCE · MP Nº 2.200-2 (Brazilian electronic signature framework), AUGUST 24, 2001
reg-identificacao.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. KYC: check CPF taxpayer registration status with Brazil's tax authority, identify the individual and representatives, and gather biometric evidence. The CPF inquiry reports registration status; tax compliance and credit scores come from their respective sources. Onboarding follows policy when further action is required. Signing: invitation, code, evidence, sealed PDF, and completion certificate form the execution record. Article 10, paragraph 2, of MP nº 2.200-2 (Brazilian electronic signature framework), August 24, 2001, permits other means of proving authorship and integrity accepted by the parties; the institution sets the appropriate assurance level for each transaction. The platform's completion certificate records signing-service evidence; an ICP-Brasil certificate, when required, belongs to the signatory. Source: MP nº 2.200-2, August 24, 2001. Article 10, paragraph 2, covers other means of establishing authorship and integrity of electronic documents when admitted as valid by the parties or accepted by the person against whom the document is presented. Official text: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/mpv/antigas_2001/2200-2.htm.
reg-dados.text09: LGPD · logs filter direct personal identifiers, retention periods are defined, and organizations are isolated. Support identifiers enable execution review; role-based access and retained evidence support accountability.
reg-dados.text12: SOURCE · LEI Nº 13.709, AUGUST 14, 2018 — LGPD (Brazil's data protection law)
reg-dados.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Lei nº 13.709, August 14, 2018, the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law), establishes purpose limitation, data minimization, security, and accountability. Articles 6, 15–16, and 46 address minimization, the end of processing purposes with applicable retention, and protection. The product filters CPF and CNPJ taxpayer IDs, Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) keys, phone numbers, and email addresses from logs. Support identifiers remain subject to access controls and are treated as personal data whenever they enable identification. Execution history: 36 months; credit history: 60 months; configurable with a 12-month minimum. These are product settings; the institution defines retention policy according to its obligations. Data, keys, and events are separated by organization. Source: Lei nº 13.709, August 14, 2018 — Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais. Scope: personal data processing and protection of freedom and privacy. Relevant provisions: data minimization, security, and accountability principles in article 6 and protective measures in article 46. Official text: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2015-2018/2018/lei/l13709.htm.
reg-lastro.text03: A signed assignment, sealed PDF, completion certificate, and transaction trail support receivables review. For FIDC, Brazilian receivables investment funds, these records support verification of underlying receivables under Resolução CVM nº 175 (Brazilian Securities Commission), December 23, 2022.
reg-lastro.text10: THE FUND MANAGER IS RESPONSIBLE FOR VERIFYING UNDERLYING RECEIVABLES
reg-lastro.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Resolução CVM nº 175 (Brazilian Securities Commission), December 23, 2022, and its Anexo Normativo II govern FIDC, Brazilian receivables investment funds, and service provider responsibilities. Operations retain documents and evidence of acquired rights to support verification of underlying receivables and applicable oversight. Assignment, signing, confirmation, and the audit trail support this work. The team links assigned rights, counterparties, and receipts; the fund manager, administrator, custodian, and registry each perform their role. Source: Resolução CVM nº 175, December 23, 2022. Scope: formation, operation, disclosure, and services for investment funds. Relevant section: Anexo Normativo II on provider responsibilities for verifying underlying receivables. Official regulation: https://conteudo.cvm.gov.br/legislacao/resolucoes/resol175.html; official consolidated Annex II: https://conteudo.cvm.gov.br/export/sites/cvm/legislacao/resolucoes/anexos/100/resol175consolid_Anexo02.pdf.
reg-garantias.text02: Collateral and CPR (rural product note) each retain their own legal steps.
reg-garantias.text03: The Marco Legal das Garantias (Brazilian collateral framework law) informs review of property records and lien priority. CPR has its own requirements and registration steps; the desk brings together documents, deadlines, filing references, covenants, and releases.
reg-garantias.text13: SOURCE · LEI Nº 14.711 (Brazilian collateral framework law), OCTOBER 30, 2023 · LEI Nº 8.929 (Brazilian rural product note law), AUGUST 22, 1994
reg-garantias.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Collateral framework: article 2 of Lei nº 14.711 (Brazilian collateral framework law), October 30, 2023, governs successive fiduciary transfers of title as security and their priority; the institution checks effectiveness and ranking at the registry. CPR (rural product note): Lei nº 8.929 (Brazilian rural product note law), August 22, 1994, covers instrument requirements, collateral, and registration or deposit, as amended. The platform assembles the document, stores its number and hash, and tracks filing references, deadlines, liens, and obligations. It organizes property records and liens in registration order for team review. Removal of adverse credit records, lien releases, and payoff documents are distinct acts, covered on the registration and release slide. Sources: Lei nº 14.711, October 30, 2023 — Marco Legal das Garantias, article 2 on effectiveness and priority of successive fiduciary transfers. Official text: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2023/lei/l14711.htm. Lei nº 8.929, August 22, 1994, establishing the Cédula de Produto Rural, articles 1 and 3 on the instrument and documentary requirements, including descriptions of pledged assets. Official text: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/leis/l8929.htm.
reg-consignado.text02: CLT · connect employment to digital lending.
reg-consignado.text03: The new rules for CLT private-sector payroll-deductible loans connect contracting, authorization, payroll registration, and deductions to public operators' systems. Operations track deduction capacity, employment status, remittances, and installment settlement.
reg-consignado.text08: DEDUCTION CAPACITY · EMPLOYMENT STATUS · REMITTANCE · INSTALLMENT SETTLEMENT
reg-consignado.text10: SOURCE · LEI Nº 15.179 (Brazilian private-sector payroll lending law), JULY 24, 2025
reg-consignado.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Lei nº 15.179 (Brazilian private-sector payroll lending law), July 24, 2025, changed digital operations for payroll-deductible loans to CLT employees. It covers deduction authorization, data-sharing consent, institution eligibility, and execution and payroll registration through public systems, using eSocial and CNIS as regulated. Each deduction is linked to the received remittance and the contract installment. The product supports employer agreement setup, deduction capacity, payroll registration records, and batch remittances; the institution manages eligibility and integration with the public operator. Payroll-deductible lending to INSS benefit recipients follows its own separately configured regime. Source: Lei nº 15.179, July 24, 2025, changing employee payroll lending through digital systems or platforms. Relevant scope: authorization, consent, eligibility, and registration in public operators' systems. Official text: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2025/lei/l15179.htm.
reg-trilhos.text02: New rails for receivables and recurring payments.
reg-trilhos.text03: Electronic trade receivables require ownership, encumbrance, and settlement checks in the authorized system. Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) supports recurring payments through Pix Automático, with authorization and lifecycle management. Platform documents, workflows, controls, and audit trails support operations.
reg-trilhos.text14: SOURCE · LEI Nº 13.775 (Brazilian electronic trade receivables law) · Resolução BCB Nº 540 (Central Bank of Brazil) · Resolução BCB Nº 505 (Central Bank of Brazil)
reg-trilhos.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Electronic trade receivables: Lei nº 13.775 (Brazilian electronic trade receivables law), December 20, 2018, and Resolução BCB nº 540 (Central Bank of Brazil), December 18, 2025, cover electronic issuance and updated rules. Ownership, encumbrances, trading, and settlement are checked with the authorized entity selected by the institution. Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) supports recurring payments through Pix Automático, with specific rules for authorization, cancellation, and status responses. Resolução BCB nº 505 (Central Bank of Brazil), September 25, 2025, updates account debit procedures; article 2-A directs payments to Pix Automático for legal-entity recipients or entities outside BCB authorization, effective October 13, 2025. Platform documents, workflows, controls, and audit trails organize work around these external rails. Sources: Lei nº 13.775, December 20, 2018, on electronic trade receivables issuance: https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2015-2018/2018/lei/l13775.htm. Resolução BCB nº 540, December 18, 2025, updating electronic trade receivables issuance, registration, deposit, and trading rules: https://www.bcb.gov.br/estabilidadefinanceira/exibenormativo?numero=540&tipo=Resolu%C3%A7%C3%A3o+BCB. Resolução BCB nº 505, September 25, 2025: https://www.bcb.gov.br/estabilidadefinanceira/exibenormativo?numero=505&tipo=Resolu%C3%A7%C3%A3o+BCB; official scope and transition notice: https://www.bcb.gov.br/detalhenoticia/20855/nota.
arquitetura.alt01: Interlocking architectural elements in purple concrete
arquitetura.text03: Channels, workflows, Decision, calculations, execution, and the desk shape the journey. Identity, organization data, and audit trails support every step through to credit operations.
arquitetura.notes: Presentation paths: 40 · 60. Read the architecture from the customer's journey. The receivables channel supports offers, simulation, assessment, proposals, and acceptance; workflows organize dependencies; Decision applies policy; calculations and execution turn terms into a contract.
